question.problem:
Consider a function $f:{R}^{3\times 2}\to {R}^{2}$ defined by

$$
f(A)=[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]A.
$$

Given that ${a}_{ij}$ denotes the entry of $A$ in the intersection of the $i$th row and $j$th column, we have

$\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{a}_{32}}=${{field-1}}.

Consider a function $\mathbf{f}: \mathbb R^{2\times 3} \to \mathbb R^2$ defined by

Given that $a_{ij}$ denotes the entry of $\mathbf{A}$ in the intersection of the $i$th row and $j$th column, find the value of $\dfrac{\partial f_1}{\partial a_{12}}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
We can write the function $\mathbf{f}$ as
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14217875/assets/23e23fe433517a6ea70c2a06f8b96983ee3c369d73a39b5c6f8a2f5dbddde203.svg)

Thus,

$$
\dfrac{\partial f_1}{\partial a_{12}} = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial a_{12}} (-a_{11} + 3a_{12} + 7a_{13} ) = 3.
$$
